thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] registers a gas-detector-family product using a Nordic SoftDevice S140 v7.2.0, working through a Component-QDID identification problem (no QDID exists explicitly for v7.2.0, resolved by tracing an End Product registration's Product List history back to a shared v7.0.1 base), a detailed explanation of why this combination produces ICS Form warning marks (a structural/versioning artifact rather than a genuine incompatibility, resolved via TCW), compliance folder logistics including accepting one representative model's documentation for a multi-model registration, guidance on keeping the public product description generic for an unreleased product, and a login/account continuity problem caused by the original registered employee leaving the company, resolved via SIG's account-recovery flow and a Receipt Number Transfer Request.
all_questions_found: The quote-request form listed SoftDevice S140 v6.1.1, but the actual firmware is v7.2.0, and no Component registration exists explicitly for S140 v7.2.0 -- how should the registration QDIDs be determined in this case?
Why does this QDID combination produce a yellow warning mark in the ICS Form?
What does 'acceptable via TCW (Test Case Waiver) application' actually mean?
What is the status of the customer's preparation of the compliance folder documents (operation manual, product block diagram, product outline drawing)?
If detailed outline drawings are only available for one of several models covered by the registration, is providing documentation for just that one model sufficient for the compliance folder?
Is the brief English product description field mandatory, and how much detail should it contain for a product that has not yet launched?
Why does the originally-submitted login account fail with an 'Invalid username or password' error, and was this caused by a SIG-side password reset requirement?
Since the originally-submitted account belonged to an employee who has since left the company and was deactivated, how should the customer proceed with a new account instead?
Since the Qualification Fee's Receipt Number is attached to the old (departed employee's) account, how can it be transferred to the customer's new account?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread demonstrates how to resolve a missing Component-level QDID for a specific firmware version: an existing End Product registration's Product List can show that a later version was added on top of an originally-registered earlier version, which means the earlier version's underlying LL/Host QDIDs represent functionality common to all the later, compatible firmware versions and can still be referenced even though no QDID exists explicitly for the exact later version. It also explains a structural cause of ICS Form warning marks: when a registration references an old QDID (registered years earlier under an older spec version), and the current registration's ICS structure has since grown new items and corresponding inter-layer dependency rules, any ICS item that did not exist at the time of the old QDID's original registration is treated as blank, which the consistency-check engine reads as 'Not Supported' -- triggering dependency-rule warnings against LL items that are themselves 'phantom' (they never existed in the old QDID's ICS at all). Since this is an artifact of ICS structure evolution rather than a genuine incompatibility, it is resolved via a TCW application rather than corrective action.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: When no Component-level QDID exists explicitly for a product's exact firmware/SoftDevice version, check whether an existing End Product registration's Product List shows that version having been added on top of an earlier originally-registered version -- if so, the earlier version's underlying QDIDs can be referenced for the new registration, since they represent functionality common across the compatible version range. When a registration referencing an old QDID produces inter-layer dependency warnings, check whether the flagged dependent items existed in the old QDID's ICS at the time of its original registration; if they did not exist (a 'phantom' inconsistency caused by the ICS structure having grown since), this is a structural artifact resolvable via TCW rather than a sign of genuine incompatibility requiring rework.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming no registration path exists simply because no Component QDID matches the exact firmware version, without checking End Product Product List history for a shared earlier-version base, could block a viable registration unnecessarily. Treating a 'phantom' inter-layer dependency warning (caused by ICS structure evolution) as a genuine incompatibility requiring redesign or retesting, rather than applying for the appropriate TCW, would waste significant effort on an unnecessary fix.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer's exact firmware/SoftDevice version has no explicit Component-level QDID, check an existing End Product registration's Product List history for a shared earlier-version base before assuming no path exists. When an old QDID reference produces inter-layer dependency warnings, determine whether the flagged items are 'phantom' -- items that did not exist in the old QDID's ICS at the time of its original registration -- since this artifact of ICS structure evolution is resolved via TCW rather than genuine rework. For multi-model registrations, accepting compliance folder documentation for one representative model, with others to follow once available, is a reasonable practice. For unreleased or sensitive products, keep the public product description generic and use the public disclosure date to control visibility timing. When a registration's login account fails, walk through SIG's Get Username / account creation / reset flow before assuming new credentials are needed, and if an account turns out to belong to a departed employee, resolve any resulting Receipt Number mismatch via a Transfer Request rather than assuming the new account already has access.
